Section: TECSACK SOFTWARE > 1. Overview

Table to Order Food App (Tap2Table) is a cross-platform application that lets diners browse a

restaurant menu, build an order and pay from a device at the table, while restaurant staff manage the

menu and process incoming orders from a companion admin app.

The same codebase produces two application flavours, Admin and User, selected by build configuration.

The User app presents the menu with images, prices and ratings, category filters and search, a cart,

payment options and an order confirmation. The Admin app provides menu and category management

and an order board with Order Requests, Current Orders and Order Completed tabs.

The application is built on .NET 9 and .NET MAUI using the MVVM pattern and targets Android, iOS, Mac

Catalyst and Windows. Menu items, categories and orders are held on the Tap2Table server and reached

through a REST API returning JSON; the server address is read from an embedded Appconfig.json file,

and the app keeps no local database.

Section: TECSACK SOFTWARE > 2. Business Context

Restaurants and cafes that take orders at the table typically need to:

• Show diners the full menu with pictures, prices, ratings and descriptions

• Let diners place and pay for an order without waiting for staff

• Give staff a live list of new orders to accept, decline or mark as delivered

• Keep the menu current: items, prices, availability, categories and cuisines

• Track every order by table, date, items, quantity, total and payment type

Table to Order Food App brings ordering, payment and order handling into two companion apps that

share one server, so a change made by the restaurant is what the diner sees, and an order placed by the

diner is what the staff see.

Section: TECSACK SOFTWARE > 4. Functional Modules > 4.1 Admin & User Application Modes

• The build configuration (Admin or User) sets the app title, application ID and start-up route, producing
Tap2Table Admin and Tap2Table User

• On launch the Admin build opens the Menu List screen and the User build opens the ordering screen;
the route also depends on whether the device is a tablet or a phone

• A top navigation bar offers Menu List, Add Menu, Orders and Menu, with the active button highlighted

Section: TECSACK SOFTWARE > 4. Functional Modules > 4.2 Menu Browsing & Search

• Menu items and categories are fetched from the server (up to 500 per request); each item shows its
image, name, price, rating and description

• Category chips, with an added “All” chip, filter the list; the search box filters items by name within the
selected category

• A toggle switches between a five-column grid and a list layout, and a message is shown when no
items are found

Section: TECSACK SOFTWARE > 4. Functional Modules > 4.3 Cart & Order Review

• Each menu item has an ADD button with plus and minus controls; reducing the quantity below one
removes the item

• View Cart opens the review screen, or shows “Please Add Food” when nothing has been added

• On the review screen quantities can be increased or decreased, more items added through an Add
Items pop-up, and the total (items plus a fixed $1.00 tax) updates instantly

Section: TECSACK SOFTWARE > 4. Functional Modules > 4.4 Payment Options

• Payment Options offers Debit/Credit Cards and Tap to Pay; selecting one clears the other

• Choosing a card opens a Card Detail form for card number, expiry (auto-formatted with a slash) and
CVV, each of which is required

• Make Payment checks that the cart is not empty, that a payment option is chosen and, for cards, that
details were entered

Section: TECSACK SOFTWARE > 4. Functional Modules > 4.5 Order Placement & Confirmation

• The order carries the table ID, UTC order date, total, payment type, a Pending order status and its line
items with food item, quantity and price

• It is posted to the server’s order API; on success a “Thank You! Your order has been placed” pop-up
shows for two seconds

• The app then returns to the menu; only the payment type is sent, not the card number, expiry or CVV

Section: TECSACK SOFTWARE > 4. Functional Modules > 4.6 Menu Management (Admin)

• Menu List shows product image, name, category, price and availability, with edit and delete options for
each item

• Add Menu captures name, price, description, category, cuisine (Indian, Chinese, Italian, Mexican,
American), availability Yes/No and a rating that defaults to 5

• Name, price above zero and description are required; edits use a pop-up with the same checks, and
delete removes the item by name and refreshes the list

Section: TECSACK SOFTWARE > 4. Functional Modules > 4.7 Category Management

• An Add New Category pop-up takes a category name and saves it to the server

• Categories are loaded from the server for the category picker and for the menu filter chips, and reload
after a new one is added

• The category service also supports read, update and delete operations

Section: TECSACK SOFTWARE > 4. Functional Modules > 4.8 Order Management (Admin)

• Order Requests lists new orders that have not been accepted; Current Orders lists accepted orders
not yet delivered; Order Completed lists delivered and canceled orders

• Each row shows order ID, date, table, food items, quantity, amount, total and payment type

• Accept moves an order to Current Orders, Decline marks it Canceled, and Delivered marks it
Completed; each change is sent to the server, and the list refreshes every 60 seconds

Section: TECSACK SOFTWARE > 6. System Architecture & Integrations

The app is organized in layers and connects to a single external service, the Tap2Table server:

• Presentation: XAML pages for the menu list, add menu, orders, menu, cart review and ordering
screens, with pop-ups (Mopups) and a bottom sheet (The49.Maui.BottomSheet), inside a Shell

• View models: MVVM view models with observable collections and commands for menu, cart,
payment, orders and category management

• Services: food item, category, order and order-management services behind interfaces, registered
with dependency injection and called through HttpClient

• Tap2Table server: REST API with FoodItem, Category and Order endpoints; lists are paged (page
number and page size) and exchanged as JSON

• Configuration: Appconfig.json is embedded in the app and read at start-up through
Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration to supply the server address

• Platform services: an Android network-availability service behind the INetwork interface

Section: TECSACK SOFTWARE > 8. Security & Data Handling

• The server address is an HTTPS URL supplied by Appconfig.json, so the environment can be
changed without changing code

• The order sent to the server carries the payment type only; the card number, expiry and CVV typed
into the Card Detail form are not part of the order

• Menu, category and order data is stored on the server; the app keeps no local database

• Forms enforce required fields: card number, expiry and CVV for card payment, and name, price and
description for menu items

• Admin and User apps are built as separate configurations with their own application IDs

• Current scope: user sign-in and role-based access control are not part of this version, so access to
admin screens relies on the Admin build

• Current scope: the service clients relax server certificate validation for the present setup, which should
be tightened before production use

Section: TECSACK SOFTWARE > 9. Value Delivered

• Lets diners order and pay from the table without waiting for staff

• Presents the menu with images, prices, ratings, categories and search so choices are quick

• Gives staff a single board to accept, decline and deliver orders, with automatic refresh

• Keeps the menu current from the admin app: items, prices, availability and categories are served from
the server

• Uses one .NET MAUI codebase for Android, iOS, Mac Catalyst and Windows, on tablets and phones

• Keeps the diner and staff apps in sync through one central server
